distractors: Genuine agreement from the people who actually have to do the work, to the point where they will argue for it when you are not there.
Advice and guidance given privately to somebody less experienced, on how to read a situation and what to do next. Nothing of the giver's own standing is put at risk by it.

Formal budget authority over a programme: the signature that releases the money and the right to stop releasing it. It is a control written into the finance process rather than anything a person chooses to spend on your behalf, and it stays with the role after the holder moves on.

Responsibility for the day-to-day delivery of a project: the person who runs the plan, chases the dependencies and is asked first when a date starts to slip. The job is to make the thing happen week by week, and it is done on organisation and follow-through rather than on any weight the person carries with the people above the programme.

A named contact who handles escalations once the normal route has failed, so that a stuck item has somewhere to go outside the usual queue. The role is a routing decision the organisation published in advance; it costs the person holding it nothing, and their name on the list carries no opinion about whether the thing being escalated deserves to succeed.
